chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Fadhl from Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Tatari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the sale of singing female slaves, so he said: 'Their purchase and their sale are forbidden, and teaching them is disbelief, and listening to them is hypocrisy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying and selling singing female slaves in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that elevates the commerce of singing slave girls from a mere transactional prohibition to a triad of spiritual defects: their trade is haram, their instruction is kufr, and their listening is nifaq. This classification underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the medium of art can corrupt the soul, linking economic activity directly to theological states of disbelief and hypocrisy.
